raw_response:
I am already thinking about money first. My land is only 30 mu, and people in the house also work outside, so I cannot spread myself too thin. I will still keep the wheat-maize rotation on most of the land because that is the steady way here. If one side is not good, at least the other side can help. Stevia can make a bit more money on good years, but it needs more hands and more careful field work, so I will not put too much area into it. This year I plan to keep 22 mu in wheat-maize rotation and 8 mu in stevia. For wheat, I will sow around the usual early October time, use the seed variety I can get locally, and put fertilizer in two times, not all at once. I do not dare cut fertilizer too much because if wheat turns yellow, yield drops fast. But I also cannot spend too much cash at the start, so I will do a middle way, about the same as the better farmers nearby, just a little careful with cost.

For maize, after wheat harvest I will move quickly. That gap is short, so I will not do heavy tillage. I will use a hybrid seed from the local dealer and get it in right after wheat comes off. If rain is decent, I will only irrigate once or maybe not much more, because pumping water costs money. For stevia, I will keep it on the smaller block. That crop needs more watching and more labor, but it can bring cash if the stand is good. I will feed it steadily, not too heavy, and irrigate when the ground gets too dry. I mostly follow what has worked on my own fields and what I see in the village: do not gamble too much, do not leave the crop hungry, and always keep some money back in hand.
